atoms.b: When an apple falls from a tree, it always falls ((++downwards sideways)) because of ((++gravity electricity)).
This very action inspired me, ((++Isaac_Newton Leonardo_da_Vinci)), an English scientist from the ((++17th_century 1st_century)).
I discovered that objects are not only pulled to the ((++centre top)) of the Earth, but also to ((++each_other the_sky)) because all objects exert gravity.

I also noted that the object’s ((++mass colour)) affects how strong this force is. I was the first person to use maths to describe the ((++relationship friendship)) between the force of gravity and mass.

instruction.text: Are the following statements true or false?

atoms.a: Newton was inspired to study gravity when an apple fell on his head, making him think of the force that pulled it down to the ground.
Newton discovered that all objects have gravity, and the strength of the force depends on the object’s colour.
Which of the following actually affects the strength of an object’s gravity?

instruction.text: Drag the Earth and the Moon to the correct places.

feedback.finish:
The Moon travels in circles around the Earth because of gravity — but why doesn’t it crash down to the ground?
The Moon is moving at the perfect speed. It moves fast enough to not fall down, but not so fast that it breaks free of Earth’s gravity. This phenomena is known as being in orbit.

atoms.a: If bigger objects exert stronger gravity, which of the following has a stronger gravitational pull?

feedback.finish: The Earth’s stronger gravitational pull is exactly what keeps the Moon in the Earth’s orbit!

atoms.a: By applying his theories of gravity, Newton hypothesised that the force that makes an apple fall from a tree is the same force that keeps the Moon in place. Was he correct?
